Values and tolerances from specs/001-shredpocalypse-bed-draft/contracts/tuning-data.md. Opening positions for playtest, not measurements. Changing a value outside its documented tolerance is a feel change: re-run the acceptance scenarios and bump rulesVersion.

2026-09-10, feature 006 (specs/006-slope-driven-speed): grounded speed is no longer a target to accelerate toward. baseSpeed, tuckSpeedMax, tuckAccel, tuckDecel and slopeAccelFactor are RETIRED and deleted rather than left unread. Speed is now produced by gravity along the slope opposed by friction and quadratic air drag, and a tuck acts by REDUCING drag rather than by raising a target - which is what a tuck actually is. Terminal velocity is emergent, so a gradient is worth whatever speed it is worth.

dragStanding and dragTucked are SOLVED, NOT CHOSEN. They are whatever makes the course's GENTLEST gradient - 0.25 - hold 2.60 standing and 4.00 tucked. Re-anchored 2026-09-10 after the first playtest: the anchor used to sit at gradient 0.30 and the course ran down to 0.20, so the gentlest ground was worth only 3.41 tucked and the player arrived at the big booter having lost 42% of the speed the steeps gave him. Anchoring at the FLOOR of the gradient range instead sets what the slowest ground is worth, which is the number the player actually feels. Editing either by hand moves that anchor and silently re-feels both courses; tests/sim/slope-response.test.ts asserts the anchor rather than the constants, so such an edit fails loudly. The ratio between them falls out at 2.61, meaning a tuck cuts drag to 38% of standing, which is a plausible figure nobody aimed at.

speedMax is a safety rail, NOT the mechanism (FR-219). It sits above the tucked terminal at CV-2's steepest legal gradient of 1.732, which is 7.504, so it never binds on any legal course. A value of 7.0 was considered and rejected for exactly that reason: it would have silently capped speed on a very steep course and turned the rail back into a target.

launchImpulseMax came down 7.2 -> 5.0 on 2026-09-04: at 7.2 a max-charge crouch release apexed at 81 against shelves standing 50 and 55, so the upper track could be entered with no ramp at all and CV-13's entry fee was optional. At 5.0 the apex is 39 - over a 16-unit log with room, under either shelf, and well under the 99 an ordinary pop ramp gives. kickerImpulseMax went 8.0 -> 10.5 -> 12.5 -> 10.0 on 2026-09-04; it came back down once booters started throwing FORWARD rather than up.

slopeFriction came 0.02 -> 0.012 in the same pass. The playtest asked for it in these words: 'snow is slippery and you can still maintain speed at a significant level going from very very steep to flat.' Correct, and worth stating what it does NOT buy: momentum. The speed time constant is 1/(2 * terminal * drag), so for a fixed top speed a LONGER response needs MORE friction, not less. Slippery snow makes speed track the slope faster. What lower friction does buy is a higher floor - the gentlest ground holds more speed - and that is why it went down. The momentum the playtest wanted comes from the course's gradient RANGE narrowing to 0.25-0.60, which is a change to data/courses, not to these numbers.

kickerImpulseMax 10.0 -> 12.0 on 2026-09-10, and the booters' gravityScale went away entirely with it. The second playtest asked for real gravity, and measured it: at gravityScale 1.0 the big booter saturated the old 10.0 cap at power 2.07 and stopped there, giving 57 ticks of air against an apex of 135 — headroom above the skier and nothing left to spend it with. The cap, not the frame, was the limit. At 12.0 the big booter reaches 4 rotations (66 ticks, apex 183) and the FRAME becomes the limit: 5 rotations needs apex 282 against a 180-tall buffer, where the ground is gone for most of the flight and the jump reads as a fall. Four is the honest ceiling at true gravity and the trick budget came 12 -> 4 to match.
